newsitem.title: BELARUS: Lukashenko claims victory in referendum.
newsitem.headline: Lukashenko claims victory in referendum.

text.p: President Alexander Lukashenko claimed victory in a controversial referendum on widening his powers in Belarus and said he would start forming a new, lower house of parliament with the existing deputies on Monday.

"Today we will set about forming the house of representatives," he told a news conference after official results showed his draft constitution had won the backing of 70.5 percent of the electorate on Sunday. "There will be no need for new elections."

Lidiya Yermoshina, head of the central electoral commission, said 70.5 percent of the entire electorate -- not just those who voted -- backed Lukashenko's draft constitution, allowing him to remodel parliament into two chambers.

Only 7.9 percent of the 7.2 million electorate backed a second constitutional draft proposed by LUkashenko's opponents in parliament which would have abolished the presidency and strengthened deputies' powers, she said.
